No `teacher` or `contenteditable` surface and no inspected `fetch(` or Supabase call was found in the current jose-study index source; therefore this audit found no in-page teacher correction/sync channel in that source.
present_human_loop.correction_roundtrip_today: HUMAN_MESSAGE -> target resolution outside page -> source/workstream edit -> validation/promotion as applicable -> student-visible route. The target-resolution and visible-result receipt are not yet one cohesive teacher UX.

findings.finding: The first missing interaction is not another editor control; it is authority-aware target resolution. 'Cambiá la página de José' can refer to a catalog-live R13 source, the later V11 lab frontier, Student World, a subject/course page or a Class Player capability surface.
findings.impact: A one-message correction can succeed technically while changing the wrong artifact or a non-served candidate.
findings.required_behavior: Resolve project/root -> child surface -> exact authority state before applying a change. Never resolve by largest version number, newest file or surface label alone.

findings.finding: The later José V11 frontier is explicitly NOT_CURRENT_NOT_SERVED while the catalog declares the older/current source route jose-study live.
findings.impact: The newest-looking design can be less visible to the student than an older source. A teacher needs the system to say which visible target will change, without forcing manual archaeology.
findings.required_behavior: Every correction receipt should name resolved target, pre-change authority class, candidate/result artifact and whether any Served pointer changed.

findings.finding: The inspected jose-study source is a student Study application with local learner state; this audit found no teacher/editor surface or network correction channel in that source.
findings.impact: There is no direct teacher-message -> page mutation -> visible receipt loop inside the current student page.
findings.required_behavior: Keep teacher correction as a control-plane/page-thread capability rather than embedding ad-hoc admin/editor logic into the student surface.

findings.finding: Learner interaction state is browser-local in the inspected jose-study source, while durable design/content authority lives in Git/Prometeo workstreams.
findings.impact: Content corrections and learner progress are different state domains and must not be conflated. A content update must preserve attempts/progress when schema compatibility allows it.
findings.required_behavior: Separate content/version receipts from learner-state migration; never clear or rewrite practice state merely because theory/content changes.

findings.finding: The current jose-study source already imports the explicit shared Study v1 owner, and recovery evidence forbids student-specific UI forks.
findings.impact: A fast teacher correction implemented as copied CSS/JS would create divergence and future regressions.
findings.required_behavior: Student-specific corrections own content/config/state; reusable behavior changes route to shared/study owner with normal compatibility rules.

findings.finding: Class Player V26/V37 evidence contains useful interaction capabilities but is not authority for the Alumnos teacher/root experience.
findings.impact: Reusing the whole Class Player UX would collapse distinct student, class, board and teacher-control identities.
findings.required_behavior: Adopt only desired proved capabilities, preserving V26 rollback stability, pressed-only eraser and typed-undo guards where applicable.

non_obvious_findings: The key UX bug is an authority-resolution bug: the system can have both a live source and a newer lab frontier, so 'latest' and 'what the student sees' are not the same coordinate.
The label `alumnos-teacher` currently names a swarm coordination surface, not a proven product page. Building a UI directly from that label would prematurely invent product identity.

A good one-message correction loop should not add an admin mode to jose-study by default; it should bridge human intent to the owning source/workstream and return a visible-result receipt while leaving the student surface simple.
preserve_invariants: José Study canonical course architecture: four distinct Algebra topics, each with its own 12-level map; 48 canonical exercises remain sourced rather than invented.
Theory scrolling must not silently mutate/destroy practice state.
Selection is not submission; diagnostic traps remain hidden before submission.
Mobile theory remains primary with practice/board in the established responsive flow; desktop keeps wheel/trackpad plus drag parity.
shared/study/current.json remains the reusable Study UI owner; student-specific products do not fork it.
Student World, subject, Study, Class/Atlas and homework remain distinct identities.
No Current/Human Accepted/Served promotion by inference.
